rv.q: Anyone who worried that Bill T. Jones’s singular, sensational show might lose its mojo in transferring to Broadway can relax.
"Fela!" is a unique Broadway experience that leaves the audience on their feet and wanting more.
Fela! is more than a musical; it's an ecstatic phenomenon.

This blazingly energetic biographical musical about the Nigerian musician and activist Fela Kuti is a sensory assault of the most welcome kind, a show that fills the theater with pulsing Afrobeat rhythms and dazzling choreography.
This is as close as Broadway gets to fully immersive theater.
This bio-musical featuring the music of the legendary African musician will have audiences dancing in the aisles.

I know I should feel hard-wired to enjoy - no, to love - "Fela!," the biography/concert/spectacle/collage about Fela Anikulapo-Kuti, the late Nigerian politico, rebel, hedonist and galvanic center of the fusion ethno-pop music known as Afrobeat.
Fela! earns its exclamation point, joyfully and relentlessly.

Like a true impresario, Fela radiates joy as he oversees the action on stage. But his players, from his activist mother (Lillias White) to a chorus of dancers gyrating to Bill T. Jones' muscular choreography, seem more self-possessed, holding the audience at a distance.

Broadway has never before witnessed a musical quite like "Fela!" — an explosive mix of catchy Afrobeat rhythms, wild, sexy dancing and raw bio-dramatics — and while its unique charms certainly are powerful, one frankly wonders whether this unusual show will catch on with the mainstream public.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this electrifying bio-musical about Nigerian musician Fela Kuti as an exuberant dance party that transforms Broadway, praising Bill T. Jones' choreography and the infectious Afrobeat score that gets audiences on their feet.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
